title: Pointwise local-ring criteria for local complete intersections
statement: Let $k$ be a field. For a scheme $X$ locally of finite type over $k$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], the following are equivalent: (1) $X$ has an affine open cover by spectra of finitely generated $k$-algebras that are local complete intersections over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field]; (2) every point $x\in X$ has an affine open neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$ such that $R$ is a global complete intersection over $k$; (3) every local ring $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is a complete-intersection local ring over $k$, meaning that it is isomorphic as a $k$-algebra to a quotient of a regular local $k$-algebra essentially of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra] by an ideal generated by a finite regular sequence [def-weil-regular-scheme, def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. For a finitely generated $k$-algebra $S$, $S$ is a local complete intersection over $k$ if and only if every localization $S_{\mathfrak p}$ at a prime ideal [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is a complete-intersection local ring over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field]. Empty schemes and zero rings are allowed.

source.place: Tag 01UG (lemma-local-complete-intersection), equivalence of (1), (2), (3), together with Algebra Tag 00SH (lemma-lci-global), equivalence of (1) and (2). The local-ring definition is Algebra Tag 00SD (definition-lci-local-ring); essentially finite type is Tag 00QM (definition-essentially-finite-p-t).

proof.text: For a finitely generated LCI $k$-algebra $S$ and a prime $\mathfrak q$, [lem-trf-lci-prime-polynomial-local-presentation] presents $S_{\mathfrak q}$ as a regular-local polynomial localization modulo a regular sequence in its maximal ideal. This is a complete-intersection local ring by [def-trf-complete-intersection-local-algebra].

Conversely suppose every $S_{\mathfrak q}$ is a complete-intersection local ring over $k$. At each prime $\mathfrak q$, [lem-trf-ci-local-ring-principal-neighbourhood] (with $F=S$, $Q=\mathfrak q$; its hypothesis is exactly this local-ring condition) gives $g_{\mathfrak q}\in S\setminus\mathfrak q$ with $S_{g_{\mathfrak q}}$ a global complete intersection over $k$. The opens $D(g_{\mathfrak q})$ cover $\operatorname{Spec}S$ since each prime belongs to its chosen open. This is the LCI definition [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field], proving the algebra equivalence. For $S=0$ use the empty cover.

For scheme (1)$\Rightarrow$(3), choose an LCI affine chart $U=\operatorname{Spec}S$ containing $x$. Step 1 gives the CI property of $S_{\mathfrak q}$. The isomorphism $S_{\mathfrak q}\cong\mathcal O_{X,x}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] sends $r/s$ to $r_xs_x^{-1}$. It preserves $k$, since the germ of the structural section of any scalar is its image in the stalk. Compose the quotient presentation with this isomorphism.

proof.text: For (3)$\Rightarrow$(2), local finite type and [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] give a finite-type affine chart $U=\operatorname{Spec}S$ at $x$. The same germ formula in [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] identifies $S_{\mathfrak q}$ with the CI stalk as a $k$-algebra. Then [lem-trf-ci-local-ring-principal-neighbourhood] gives $g\in S\setminus\mathfrak q$ with $S_g$ global complete intersection. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime], $D_U(g)$ is affine, contains $x$, and has coordinate ring $S_g$. Its restriction map preserves the structural scalars, so this is the required $k$-affine neighbourhood.

proof.text: For (2)$\Rightarrow$(1), the neighbourhoods cover $X$; a global complete intersection is finitely generated and LCI by [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field], using $D(1)=\operatorname{Spec}R$ and $R_1\cong R$. Thus (1)$\Rightarrow$(3)$\Rightarrow$(2)$\Rightarrow$(1). For the empty scheme all pointwise assertions and the empty affine cover are valid.
